etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin historicus (“historical”), from Ancient Greek ἱστορικός (historikós, “exact; historical”). Cognate with French historique. By surface analysis, history +‎ -ic.

definitions.definition: Very important; noteworthy: having importance or significance in history.

quote.citation: 2022 December 19, Patrick Greenfield, Phoebe Weston, “Cop15: historic deal struck to halt biodiversity loss by 2030”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: Alongside the nature targets, countries reached a historic agreement to develop a financial mechanism for sharing the benefits from drug discoveries, vaccines and food products that come from digital forms of biodiversity, known as digital sequence information or DSI, after rows about biopiracy in the lead-up to Cop15.

quote.citation: 1756 August, Horace Walpole, letter republished in Private Correspondence (1820), Vol. II, No. 1:
quote.text: Sights are thick sown in the counties of York and Nottingham: the former is more historic.

definitions.definition: (now uncommon) Synonym of historical: of, concerning, or in accordance with recorded history or the past generally (See usage notes.)

quote.citation: 1594, John Dickenson, Arisbas, Euphues amidst his slumbers; or, Cupids iourney to hell:
quote.text: An high-pac'd Muse treading a lofty march, leades honor enchaind in an Epique pen, grac'd with the furtherance of historique Clio.

definitions.definition: (grammar) Various grammatical tenses and moods specially used in retelling past events.
(obsolete) A history, a non-fiction account of the past.

quote.citation: 1566, William Painter, chapter XI, in The Palace of Pleasure Beautified, volume I:
quote.text: Before the beginnyng of this historic, I haue thought good by waie of a Proeme, to introduce the wordes of an excellent writer called Lodouicus Caelius Rhodoginus.
